messages:
Maria: vuln scanner flagged the backup-uploader service account with KMS Decrypt on the prod backups key. exact finding: privileged_grant -> grantee: serviceAccount:backup-uploader@redwood-prod.urgent, resource: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/backups/cryptoKeys/prod-backups
Kevin: confirmed. scanner (sec-scan v2) flagged it at 2026-03-21T14:02Z, sample log shows Decrypts from that principal starting 2026-03-19. link to findings: https://sec-portal/reports/INC-2026-0427
Sasha: tagging oncall. short assessment: do we know if those Decrypts correspond to legitimate restores or a misconfigured uploader that decrypts before upload? @Devon any infra context?
Devon: the uploader should never need KMS Decrypt in prod — it should upload already-encrypted blobs. sounds like a misconfig in the new multi-region uploader rollout. likely upload agent is doing local encryption for staging and we accidentally promoted that image without toggling encrypt-only mode.
Maria: agreed. immediate mitigation checklist:
 - revoke any active grants to backup-uploader principal
 - restrict its IAM to deny kms:Decrypt and leave kms:Encrypt if needed for staging
 - rotate prod CMK if we detect unauthorized decrypts (or create a new key alias and re-encrypt if required)
 - run canary restores from encrypted snapshots to verify restore path
 - update audit alerts for KMS Decrypt by non-restore principals
Kevin: I'm going to revoke the grant now and create a short-lived emergency grant for the service account if a restore is in progress. running (AWS example):
```
# list grants
aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/prod-backups
# retire grant (if we have grantId)
aws kms retire-grant --grant-id <GRANT_ID> --key-id alias/prod-backups
# revoke policy binding (GCP example)
gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding prod-backups --location global --keyring backups --member=\"serviceAccount:backup-uploader@redwood-prod.urgent\" --role=\"roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter\"
```
Sasha: I'm patching the uploader deployment to pull the previous image and pausing the rollout. `kubectl -n backups set image deploy/uploader uploader=repo/uploader:v2026-03-12` then scale to 0 for quick stop if needed.
encops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0427 created and routed to sec-eng, enc-ops. Priority: high.
Maria: who will own key rotation decision? rotation has operational cost — re-encrypting archives, cross-account grants, and canary runs. propose: rotate if we see >1 unauthorized Decrypt or evidence of exfil. otherwise revoke grant + patch uploader + audit + follow-up full infra review.
Devon: ops impact note: rotating CMK will require updating key alias in backup restore lambdas and can incur short windows where old snapshots cannot be decrypted until rekey job completes. we should schedule during low-traffic and run staged rewraps.
Kevin: evidence so far: 3 Decrypt calls from backup-uploader over 48h, but they were small metadata blobs, not full backups. not definitive for exfil. I will pull CloudTrail/GCP Audit logs and correlate with uploader pod logs. queries:
 - AWS CloudTrail: `eventSource=kms.amazonaws.com AND eventName=Decrypt AND userIdentity.arn=arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/backup-uploader`
 - GCP: `resource.type=kms_key AND protoPayload.methodName=\"Decrypt\" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"backup-uploader@redwood-prod.urgent\"`
Maria: add SIEM alert: create rule to trigger on kms:Decrypt for principals not in allowed-restorer-group. link rule: https://siem/internal/rules/backup-kms-decrypt
Sasha: I've revoked the uploader's KMS role and rolled back the deployment. steps completed: revoke IAM binding, patch deployment, scale to 0. timestamp: 2026-03-21T14:18Z. still need to rotate secret keys and confirm no pending restore jobs.
Kevin: collected logs and uploaded to sec-bucket for triage: gs://sec-evidence/INC-2026-0427/ — payloads are small. creating a forensic snapshot of affected pods and node images.
Devon: quick Terraform follow-up: we'll remove `backup-writers` group from being granted `kms:Decrypt` and add a new `backup-restorer` role scoped to restoration services only, with tight resource conditions (only specific key versions and only from our restore pipeline VPC). I'll open a PR referencing INC-2026-0427.
Maria: follow-ups/todo (owners):
 - Kevin: full log correlation + decide on rotation (ETA 2h)
 - Devon: terraform RBAC change PR + tests (ETA EOD)
 - Sasha: verify there are no in-flight restores and run canary restore (ETA 4h)
 - sec-eng: update playbook to include this class of misconfig and add detection rule (ETA 48h)
encops-bot: INC-2026-0427 status updated -> mitigated (revoked grants, rollback), next steps: validation
Sasha: canary restore started against a small snapshot (id snap-20260315-min) — will report success/failure.
Kevin: decision: rotate CMK? leaning no unless we see exfil. I'll update once correlation completes.
Maria: thanks all. once we close, add a short postmortem in #postmortems and tag this incident. also ensure backup uploader CI has a gating check preventing promotion if KMS mode != server-side-only.
Kevin: final note for audit logs: enable KMS key-level logging to SIEM with 90d retention and ensure logs include principal and request/response size. I'll open ticket.
Sasha: canary restore succeeded. no data loss observed. marking operational mitigations complete.
Maria: closing for now — set follow-up to security backlog for RBAC hardening. good work. :thumbsup:
